Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. Andy Balbirnie and Ross Adair will be the openers for Ireland. Tendai Chatara will start the proceedings with the ball for Zimbabwe.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Ireland have done a good job with the ball to restrict Zimbabwe and the onus is now on their batters to chase down this total. Will they chase it down and keep the series alive? We will find out shortly. Back in a bit for the chase..

Opting to bowl first, Ireland started with spin and were rewarded with an early wicket. However, they failed to keep the pressure on and leaked a lot of runs in the middle overs. At the halfway mark, Ireland were on course to chase a huge total but they clawed their way back into the game with some quick wickets. They kept chipping in with wickets at regular intervals and did not allow Zimbabwe to maximize in the back end of the innings. Graham Hume was the pick of the bowlers for Ireland with figures of 3 for 17 from his four overs. Harry Tector took a couple of wickets while Mark Adair and Gareth Delany chipped in with a wicket each.

Zimbabwe fail to finish on a high and end up with a below-par total on the board.  Sent into bat first, Zimbabwe were off to a solid start despite losing an early wicket. At 86-3, they were going along nicely and looked set to post a daunting total. However, the dismissal of Craig Ervine triggered a mini collapse and the hosts lost their way from thereon. Brad Evans did strike some lusty blows towards the end but he was unable to bat till the end.

GONE!! CAUGHT! Zimbabwe are bowled out for 144 from the final ball of the innings! Length ball on off, Wellington Masakadza goes for the big one, gets the height but not the distance as Harry Tector runs around at the long-on boundary and takes it brilliantly.
Commentary.Howout: c Harry Tector b Graham Hume

We are all set for the action to start. The umpires and players make their way out in the middle. Innocent Kaia and Tadiwanashe Marumani will be the openers for Zimbabwe. Harry Tector will start the proceedings with the ball for Ireland.

Craig Ervine, the skipper of Zimbabwe, says that he was not sure what would a good score be on this track. Adds that they will now look to put up a score and defend it. Feels that they had a scrappy last game but it was good to end up on the winning side. Feels that this one is a slightly better wicket and it might get slow later. Informs that Gary Ballance misses this game due to concussion and he will be replaced by Innocent Kaia.

Andy Balbirnie, the skipper of Ireland, says that they will bowl first. Adds that bowling first will give them a chance to assess the wicket well and then chase the target. Says that the wicket played well for the entire 40 overs but Zimbabwe played well and got over them. Says that it’s good to have multiple bowling options and will the captain’s choices in difficult situations. Informs that Graham Hume comes in for Barry McCarthy as the only change in the side.

PITCH REPORT - Darlington Matambanadzo is near the deck. He shares that it is a dry surface and adds that there are cracks that have widened. Feels that these are good batting conditions. Reckons that 160 should be the minimum score for the team batting first.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Ross Adair, Andy Balbirnie (C), Stephen Doheny (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Tyrone Kane, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Fionn Hand, Graham Hume (In for Barry McCarthy).

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Innocent Kaia (In for Gary Ballance), Tadiwanashe Marumani, Craig Ervine (C), Wesley Madhevere, Sean Williams, Ryan Burl, Clive Madande (WK), Brad Evans, Wellington Masakadza, Richard Ngarava, Tendai Chatara.
TOSS – The coin toss lands in the favour of Ireland and they have opted to BOWL first.

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, will take a lot of confidence from their opening game and will look to put up a similar show today that will hand them a series win. Their bowlers were right on top from the start and kept picking wickets at regular intervals. Ryan Burl was the star of the attack with 3 for 29 from his four overs. The chase started slowly and they lost a few wickets upfront but Gary Ballance and Sean Williams batted sensibly through the middle and got them over the line. Will the hosts take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series or will we see the visitors making it 1-1?  We shall find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

Having been sent into bat first in the first T20I, Ireland could never really get going in their batting effort. Gareth Delany, Stephen Doheny and Curtis Campher got into double figures but could not carry on. As a result, they were bundled out for a paltry total of 114. Their bowlers did put up a fight and made the run-scoring difficult for the Zimbabwe batters. Harry Tector and Mark Adair were the positives for them with the ball taking 2 wickets each. Irish fans will hope for a much better display with the bat and a win that will keep them alive in the series.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 2nd T20I in the 3-match T20I series between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club in Harare. The hosts got over the line in the first game as they chased down the modest total of 114 in 18 overs for the loss of 5 wickets. They will look to wrap the series with a win in this game while the visitors will look to force a series decider.
... MATCH DAY …

It is now time for the second T20I between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club in Harare. The hosts started the three-game series in fine fashion as they bulldozed the opposition and got to the finish line, taking a crucial 1-0 lead in the series. Zimbabwe have a great opportunity to continue the same form and kill the series with a game to spare. Ireland on the other hand have been handicapped a bit in the batting department and will need to play to the best of their abilities to get the series back on level terms. In the first game, Zimbabwe assessed the conditions well and it was an all-round performance with the ball. The pacers, especially Tendai Chatara bowled well but it was really the efforts of the spinners, Ryan Burl and Wellington Masakadza that got the opposition batters in a fix. With the bat though, the hosts' top order also faltered but the cool and experienced head of Sean Williams proved to be decisive for them. Ireland were out of sorts with the bat but with the ball, they showed a lot of fight. Harry Tector was surprisingly good with his off-breaks and their frontline pacer Mark Adair was on top of his game as well. If the batters are able to do well, then the visitors will have a good shot of winning this game. The conditions in Harare do offer a bit to the bowlers and the batters will have to be watchful before they can play the big shots. All in all, it should be an exciting watch. Who are you backing?
